quote: Is there anybody else on the title but you? Oh, do you already have solar?
stewart_read: Rep asks the co-owner question but immediately stacks a second question on top and never returns to get a clear answer — 'I do. Yes.' at 00:48 is ambiguous as to which question it answers.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep deprioritized co-owner because the orphaned-solar branch took over the conversation. Rejected — co-owner status matters for the appointment regardless of solar status, and it was never revisited.
coaching_implication: Isolate one question at a time; if co-owner is unclear, re-ask before button-up so the closer knows if a spouse needs to be on the call.

quote: And your panels, are you in contract with somebody, or are you independent?
stewart_read: Customer reveals a prior installer relationship and dissatisfaction context ("they only do Tesla Powerwalls") but rep never asks which company or why he's now shopping elsewhere.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep is focused on qualifier checklist completion, not probing competitive context. This is supported — no follow-up question about the company name appears anywhere in the call.
coaching_implication: A quick 'who was that with?' would surface competitive intel and deepen rapport with minimal time cost.

stewart_read: Customer explicitly wants brand flexibility beyond Tesla Powerwall and describes technical specificity (EG4, 48V hybrid) — a highly qualified, motivated battery buyer.
coaching_implication: This is a strong signal to reflect back ('sounds like you want more flexibility than a single-brand system') to build rapport before redirecting to specialist — rep redirects correctly later but doesn't acknowledge the specificity in the moment.

quote: do y'all do the, like, the e g four batteries?
stewart_read: This is actually a scope-hold SUCCESS, not creep — flagged here to highlight the positive contrast: rep does not attempt to answer the technical EG4 question and defers to specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read would call this a missed opportunity to sound knowledgeable, but the strategic hold is correct per schema — setter should not answer closer-tier technical content.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the model behavior for the rep — 'we have tons of batteries... I'm gonna get you a call with a specialist' is the right move, keep doing this.

quote: How much are you spending on a monthly average?
stewart_read: Bill captured at $100/month but never flipped or referenced again — no acknowledgment of whether that's high/low, no tie to the battery/storage motivation.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since customer's stated interest is storage/backup, not bill savings, the standard bill-pain flip may not apply cleanly here. Partially supported — customer's motivation is technical/resilience, not cost pain — but the bill number could still have been used as a data point for the specialist handoff.
coaching_implication: Even on a battery-only lead, restate the number to the customer as context ('at $100/month you're already pretty efficient — the specialist will factor that into sizing') rather than letting it disappear.

quote: do you want me to text you any details on what I'm looking for?
stewart_read: Customer proactively offers to send extra detail ahead of the appointment — a strong signal of investment in the process.
coaching_implication: Rep's response ('it'll always help') is fine but generic; could have tied it back to the EG4/48V hybrid specifics mentioned earlier to show the details were heard and mattered.
